newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares ease, market unsure on direction.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares ease, market unsure on direction.

text.p: Leading Russian shares closed slightly down in moderate trading on Thursday, and traders said they were divided on where the market would go next.
"There's quite a bit of support and not much reason for more agressive sales, but at the same time the market is not ready to rise," said Dmitry Starenko, senior trader at Regent European Securities.
He said market movements over the past few days indicated its volatility rather than any definite trend.
The Russian Trading System 23-share index closed down at 298.24 from Wednesday's close of 303.34 on total market volume of $29.5 million.

"Today was just a little recoil after a bit of overheating yesterday. There's big interest in 'blue chips' now and second tier shares also started moving yesterday (Wednesday)," said senior Creditanstalt-Grant trader Andrei Galperin.
He said a gradual rise in the market had already begun and predicted prices would continue up next week.
But other traders said the market was still waiting to see if the U.S. Federal Reserve might raise interest rates again and for further clarification of government plans for natural monopolies.
Starenko said investors were also waiting for more 1996 company results to be announced. Results are expected after annual shareholders' meetings typically held around this time of the year.
Mining concern Norilsk Nickel shares closed at $5.10 after plunging about 14 percent at one stage during the day to $4.65 from Wednesday's close of $5.40.

Company officials said the drop may have been connected with the completion of the distribution to company workers of a 10 percent packet of shares previously held by a special fund set up for employees.

Market bellwether UES, which has led shares higher for the past few days on announcements of details of government plans to tighten control over the company, closed at $0.2080, down slightly from $0.2100 on Wednesday.

Russia's biggest oil company LUKoil's LKOH.RTS shares also closed down at $13.57 from $13.80 previously, despite a company announcement today that net profits rose to 3.87 trillion roubles in 1996 from 2.40 trillion in 1995.
